source_text: Ac per hoc, nec aliquod peccatum [naturae in] esse, tam Conditoris humani generis quam Redemptoris testimonio comprobatur.
pass_a_gloss: And through this, that neither is any sin in nature, is proved as much by the testimony of the Founder of the human race as of the Redeemer.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Consequently, the testimony of both the Creator and the Redeemer of the human race proves that no sin exists in nature.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
